18.13: And they went thence unto mount Ephraim, and came to the house of Michah.
18.14: Then answered the five men, that went to spie out the countrey of Laish, and said unto their brethren, Know ye not, that there is in these houses an Ephod, and Teraphim, and a graven and a molten image? Now therefore consider what ye have to doe.
18.15: And they turned thitherward and came to the house of the yong man the Levite, even unto the house of Michah, and saluted him peaceably.
18.16: And the six hundreth men appointed with their weapons of war, which were of the children of Dan, stood by the entring of the gate.
18.17: Then the five men that went to spie out the land, went in thither, and took the graven image and the Ephod, and the Teraphim, and the molten image: and the Priest stood in the entring of the gate with the six hundreth men, that were appointed with weapons of war,
18.18: And the other went into Michahs house and fet the graven image, the Ephod, and the Teraphim, and the molten image. Then said the Priest unto them, What doe ye?
18.19: And they answered him, Hold thy peace: lay thine hand upon thy mouth, and come with us to be our father and Priest. Whether is it better that thou shouldest be a Priest unto ye house of one man, or that thou shouldest be a Priest unto a tribe and to a familie in Israel?
18.20: And the Priestes heart was glad, and hee took the Ephod and the Teraphim, and the graven image, and went among the people.
18.21: And they turned and departed, and put the children, and the cattell, and the substance before them.
18.22: When they were far off from the house of Michah, the men that were in the houses neere to Michahs house, gathered together, and pursued after the children of Dan,
18.23: And cryed unto the children of Dan: who turned their faces, and said unto Michah, What ayleth thee, that thou makest an outcrie?
18.24: And hee said, Yee have taken away my gods, which I made, and the Priest, and go your wayes: and what have I more? how then say ye unto me, what ayleth thee?
18.25: And the children of Dan sayde unto him, Let not thy voyce be heard among us, least angrie fellowes runne upon thee, and thou lose thy life with the lives of thine housholde.
18.26: So the children of Dan went their wayes: and when Michah saw that they were too strong for him, hee turned, and went back unto his house.
18.27: And they took the things which Michah had made, and the Priest which he had, and came unto Laish, unto a quiet people and without mistrust, and smote them with the edge of the sword, and burnt the citie with fire:
18.28: And there was none to help, because Laish was far from Zidon, and they had no business with other men: also it was in the valley that lyeth by Beth-rehob. After, they built the citie, and dwelt therein,
18.29: And called the name of the citie Dan, after the name of Dan their father which was borne unto Israel: howbeit the name of the city was Laish at the beginning.
18.30: Then the children of Dan set them up the graven image: and Jonathan the sonne of Gershom, the sonne of Manasseh and his sonnes were the Priestes in the tribe of the Danites until the day of the captiuitie of the land.
18.31: So they set them up the graven image, which Michah had made, all the while the house of God was in Shiloh.

19.1: Also in those dayes, when there was no king in Israel, a certain Levite dwelt on the side of mount Ephraim, and took to wife a concubine out of Beth-lehem Judah,
19.2: And his concubine played ye whore there, and went away from him unto her fathers house to Beth-lehem Judah, and there continued the space of four moneths.
19.3: And her husband arose and went after her, to speak friendly unto her, and to bring her again: he had also his servant with him, and a couple of asses: and she brought him unto her fathers house, and when the yong womans father saw him, he reioyced of his coming.
19.4: And his father in law, the yong womans father reteined him: and he abode with him three dayes: so they did eat and drink, and lodged there.
19.5: And when the fourth day came, they arose earely in the morning, and he prepared to depart: then the yong womans father said unto his sonne in law, Comfort thine heart with a morsel of bread, and then go your way.
19.6: So they sat down, and did eat and drink both of them together. And the yong womans father said unto the man, Be content, I pray thee, and tary all night, and let thine heart be merie.
19.7: And when the man rose up to depart, his father in law was earnest: therefore he returned, and lodged there.
19.8: And he arose up earely the fifth day to depart, and the yong womans father said, Comfort thine heart, I pray thee: and they taryed until after midday, and they both did eat.
19.9: Afterward when the man arose to depart with his concubine and his servant, his father in law, the yong womans father said unto him, Behold now, the day draweth toward even: I pray you, tary all night: behold, the sunne goeth to rest: lodge here, that thine heart may be merie, and to morowe get you earely upon your way, and goe to thy tent.
19.10: But the man would not tarry, but arose and departed, and came over against Jebus, (which is Jerusalem) and his two asses laden, and his concubine were with him.
19.11: When they were neere to Jebus, the day was sore spent, and the servant said unto his master, Come, I pray thee, and let us turn into this citie of the Jebusites, and lodge all night there.
19.12: And his master answered him, We will not turn into the citie of strangers that are not of the children of Israel, but we will goe forth to Gibeah.
19.13: And he said unto his servant, Come, and let us draw neere to one of these places, that wee may lodge in Gibeah or in Ramah.
19.14: So they went forward upon their way, and the sunne went down upon them neere to Gibeah, which is in Beniamin.
19.15: Then they turned thither to goe in and lodge in Gibeah: and when he came, he sat him down in a street of the citie: for there was no man that took them into his house to lodging.
19.16: And behold, there came an old man from his work out of the field at even, and the man was of mount Ephraim, but dwelt in Gibeah: and the men of the place were the children of Iemini.
19.17: And when he had lift up his eyes, he saw a wayfairing man in the streetes of the citie: then this old man sayde, Whither goest thou, and whence camest thou?
19.18: And hee answered him, Wee came from Beth-lehem Judah, unto the side of Mout Ephraim: from thence am I: and I went to Beth-lehem Judah, and go now to the house of the Lord: and no man receiveth mee to house,
19.19: Although we have straw and prouader for our asses, and also bread and wine for me and thine handmayde, and for the boy that is with thy servant: we lack nothing.
19.20: And the old man sayde, Peace bee with thee: as for all that thou lackest, shalt thou find with me: onely abide not in the street al night.
19.21: So he brought him into his house, and gave fodder unto the asses: and they washed their feet, and did eat and drink.
19.22: And as they were making their hearts merie, behold, the men of the citie, wicked men beset the house round about, and smote at the door, and spake to this old man the master of the house saying, Bring forth the man that came into thine house that we may know him.
19.23: And this man the master of ye house went out unto the, and said unto them, Nay my brethre, do not so wickedly, I pray you: seeing that this man is come into mine house, do not this villenie.
19.24: Behold, here is my daughter, a virgin, and his concubine: them wil I bring out now, and humble them, and doe with them what seemeth you good: but to this man doe not this villenie.
19.25: But the men would not hearken to him: therefore ye man took his concubine, and brought her out unto them: and they knew her and abused her all the night unto the morning: and when the day began to spring, they let her goe.
19.26: So the woman came in the dawning of the day, and fell down at the door of the mans house where her Lord was, till the light day.
19.27: And her lord arose in the morning, and opened the doores of the house, and went out to goe his way, and behold, the woman his concubine was dead at the door of the house and her handes lay upon the threshold.
19.28: And hee said unto her, Up and let us goe: but she answered not. Then he took her up upon the ass, and the man rose up, and went unto his place.
19.29: And whe he was come to his house, he took a knife, and laid hand on his concubine, and deuided her in pieces with her bones into twelve parts, and sent her through all quarters of Israel.
19.30: And all that saw it, said, There was no such thing done or seen since the time that the children of Israel came up from the land of Egypt unto this day: consider the matter, consult and give sentence.

20.1: Then all the children of Israel went out, and the Congregation was gathered together as one man, from Dan to Beersheba, with the land of Gilead, unto the Lord in Mizpeh.
20.2: And the chief of all the people, and all the tribes of Israel assembled in the Congregation of the people of God four hundreth thousand footemen that drew sword.
20.3: (Now the children of Beniamin heard that the children of Israel were gone up to Mizpeh) Then the children of Israel said, How is this wickedness committed?
20.4: And the same Levite, the womans husband that was slain, answered and said, I came unto Gibeah that is in Beniamin with my concubine to lodge,
20.5: And the men of Gibeah arose against me, and beset the house round about upon mee by night, thinking to have slain me, and have forced my concubine that she is dead.
20.6: Then I took my concubine, and cut her in pieces, and sent her throughout all the countrey of the inheritance of Israel: for they have committed abomination and villenie in Israel.
20.7: Behold, ye are al children of Israel: give your advise, and counsel herein.
20.8: Then all the people arose as one man, saying, There shall not a man of us goe to his tent, neither any turn into his house.
20.9: But now this is that thing which we will do to Gibeah: we wil goe up by lot against it,
20.10: And we wil take ten men of the hundreth throughout al the tribes of Israel, and an hundreth of the thousand, and a thousand of ten thousand to bring vitaile for the people that they may do (when they come to Gibeah of Beniamin) according to all the villeny, that it hath done in Israel.
20.11: So all the men of Israel were gathered against the citie, knit together, as one man.
20.12: And the tribes of Israel sent men through al the tribe of Beniamin, saying, What wickedness is this that is committed among you?
20.13: Now therefore deliver us those wicked men which are in Gibeah, that we may put them to death, and put away evil from Israel: but the children of Beniamin would not obey the voyce of their brethren the children of Israel.
20.14: But ye children of Beniamin gathered them selves together out of the cities unto Gibeah, to come out and fight against the children of Israel.
20.15: And ye children of Beniamin were nombred at that time out of the cities six and twenty thousand men that drew sword, beside the inhabitants of Gibeah, which were nombred seven hundreth chosen men.
20.16: Of all this people were seven hundreth chosen men, being left handed: all these could sling stones at an hear breadth, and not fail.
20.17: Also the men of Israel, beside Beniamin, were nombred four hundreth thousand men that drew sword, even all men of war.
20.18: And the children of Israel arose, and went up to the house of God, and asked of God, saying, Which of us shall goe up first to fight against the children of Beniamin? And the Lord said, Judah shalbe first.
20.19: Then the children of Israel arose up earely and camped against Gibeah.
20.20: And the men of Israel went out to battell against Beniamin, and the men of Israel put themselves in aray to fight against the beside Gibeah.
20.21: And the children of Beniamin came out of Gibeah, and slew down to the ground of the Israelites that day two and twentie thousand men.
20.22: And the people, the men of Israel plucked up their hearts, and set their battel again in aray in the place where they put them in aray the first day.
20.23: (For the children of Israel had gone up and wept before the Lord unto the evening, and had asked of the Lord, saying, Shall I goe again to battel against the children of Beniamin my brethren? and the Lord said, Go up against them)
20.24: Then the children of Israel came neere against the children of Beniamin the second day.
20.25: Also the second day Beniamin came forth to meet them out of Gibeah, and slew down to the ground of the children of Israel again eighteen thousand men: all they could handle the sword.
20.26: Then al the children of Israel went up and all the people came also unto the house of God, and wept and sat there before the Lord and fasted that day unto the evening, and offred burnt offrings and peace offrings before the Lord.
20.27: And the children of Israel asked the Lord (for there was the Ark of the couenat of God in those dayes,
20.28: And Phinehas the sonne of Eleazar, the sonne of Aaron stood before it at that time) saying, Shall I yet goe anie more to battel against the children of Beniamin my brethren, or shall I cease? And the Lord said, Go up: for to morowe I will deliver them into your hand.
20.29: And Israel set men to lie in wait round about Gibeah.
20.30: And the children of Israel went up against the children of Beniamin the third day, and put theselues in aray against Gibeah, as at other times.
20.31: Then the children of Beniamin coming out against the people, were drawen from the citie: and they began to smite of ye people and kill as at other times, even by the wayes in the field (whereof one goeth up to the house of God, and the other to Gibeah) upon a thirtie men of Israel.
20.32: (For the children of Beniamin sayd, They are fallen before us, as at the first. But the children of Israel said, Let us flee and pluck them away from the citie unto the hie wayes)
20.33: And all the men of Israel rose up out of their place, and put themselves in aray at Baal-tamar: and the men that lay in wayte of the Israelites came forth of their place, even out of the medowes of Gibeah,
20.34: And they came over against Gibeah, ten thousand chosen men of all Israel, and the battell was sore: for they knew not that the evil was neere them.
20.35: And the Lord smote Beniamin before Israel, and the children of Israel destroyed of the Beniamites the same day five and twenty thousand and an hundreth men: all they could handle the sword.
20.36: So the children of Beniamin saw that they were striken down: for the men of Israel gave place to the Beniamites, because they trusted to the men that lay in wait, which they had laid beside Gibeah.
20.37: And they that lay in wait hasted, and brake forth toward Gibeah, and the ambushment drew themselves along, and smote all the citie with the edge of the sword.
20.38: Also the men of Israel had appoynted a certain time with the ambushmentes, that they should make a great flame and smoke rise up out of the citie.
20.39: And when the men of Israel retired in the battel, Beniamin began to smite and kill of the men of Israel about thirtie persons: for they said, Surely they are striken down before us, as in the first battell.
20.40: But when the flame bega to arise out of the citie, as a pillar of smoke, the Beniamites looked back, and behold, the flame of the citie began to ascend up to heaven.
20.41: Then the men of Israel turned again, and the men of Beniamin were astonied: for they saw that evil was neere unto them.
20.42: Therefore they fled before the men of Israel unto the way of the wilderness, but the battell overtook them: also they which came out of the cities, slew them among them.
20.43: Thus they compassed the Beniamites about, and chased them at ease, and ouerranne them, even over against Gibeah on the Eastside.
20.44: And there were slain of Beniamin eyghteene thousad men, which were all men of war.
20.45: And they turned and fled to the wildernes unto the rock of Rimmon: and the Israelites glayned of them by the way five thousand men, and pursued after them unto Gidom, and slew two thousand men of them,
20.46: So that all that were slayne that day of Beniamin, were five and twentie thousand men that drew sword, which were all men of war:
20.47: But six hundreth men turned and fled to the wilderness unto the rock of Rimmon, and abode in the rock of Rimmon four moneths.
20.48: Then the men of Israel returned unto the children of Beniamin, and smote them with the edge of the sword from the men of the citie unto the beasts, and all that came to hand: also they set on fire all the cities that they could come by.

21.1: Moreover, the men of Israel sware in Mizpeh, saying, None of us shall give his daughter unto the Beniamites to wyfe.
21.2: And the people came unto ye house of God and abode there till even before God, and lift up their voyces, and wept with great lamentation,
21.3: And sayde, O Lord God of Israel, why is this come to pass in Israel, that this day one tribe of Israel should want?
21.4: And on the morow the people rose up and made there an altar, and offred burnt offrings and peace offrings.
21.5: Then the children of Israel said, Who is he among all the tribes of Israel, that came not up with the Congregation unto the Lord? for they had made a great othe concerning him that came not up to the Lord to Mizpeh, saying, Let him die the death.
21.6: And the children of Israel were sory for Beniamin their brother, and said, There is one tribe cut off from Israel this day.
21.7: How shall we do for wives to them that remain, seeing we have sworn by the Lord, that we will not give them of our daughters to wives?
21.8: Also they said, Is there any of the tribes of Israel that came not up to Mizpeh to the Lord? and behold, there came none of Jabesh Gilead unto the host and to the Congregation.
21.9: For when the people were vewed; behold, none of the inhabitants of Jabesh Gilead were there.
21.10: Therefore the Congregation sent thither twelve thousand men of the most valiant, and commanded them, saying, Goe, and smite the inhabitants of Jabesh Gilead with the edge of the sword, both women, and children.
21.11: And this is it that ye shall do: ye shall utterly destroy all the males and all the women that have lien by men.
21.12: And they found among the inhabitants of Jabesh Gilead four hundreth maides, virgins that had known no man by lying with any male: and they brought them unto the host to Shiloh, which is in the land of Canaan.
21.13: Then the whole Congregation sent and spake with the children of Beniamin that were in the rock of Rimmon, and called peaceably unto them:
21.14: And Beniamin came again at that time, and they gave them wives which they had saved alive of the women of Jabesh Gilead: but they had not so ynough for them.
21.15: And the people were sorie for Beniamin, because the Lord had made a breach in the tribes of Israel.
21.16: Therefore the Elders of the Congregation said, How shall we doe for wives to the remnant? for the women of Beniamin are destroyed.
21.17: And they said, there must be an inheritance for them that be escaped of Beniamin, that a tribe be not destroyed out of Israel.
21.18: Howbeit we may not give them wives of our daughters: for the childre of Israel had sworn, saying, Cursed be he that giveth a wise to Beniamin.
21.19: Therefore they said, Behold, there is a feast of the Lord every yere in Shiloh in a place, which is on the Northside of Beth-el, and on the Eastside of the way that goeth up from Beth-el to Shechem, and on the South of Lebonah.
21.20: Therefore they commanded the children of Beniamin, saying, Goe, and lye in wait in the vineyardes.
21.21: And when ye see that the daughters of Shiloh come out to dance in dances, then come ye out of the vineyards, and catch you every man a wife of the daughters of Shiloh, and goe into the land of Beniamin.
21.22: And when their fathers or their brethren come unto us to complain, we wil say unto them, Have pitie on them for our sakes, because we reserved not to eche man his wife in the war, and because ye have not given unto them hitherto, ye have sinned.
21.23: And the children of Beniamin did so, and took wives of them that danced according to their nomber: which they took, and went away, and returned to their inheritance, and repaired the cities and dwelt in them.
21.24: So the children of Israel departed thence at that time, every man to his tribe, and to his familie, and went out from thence every man to his inheritance.
21.25: In those dayes there was no King in Israel, but every man did that which was good in his eyes.
